situation: An nWave repo whose board still carries slice cards under retired rules: 4 open cards are slices of one feature, properly parented to it. Every count in the snapshot is inflated by 3.
expected_guard: one line reports that the counts are inflated by slice cards and names `/phil:groom-set` as what resolves it; the snapshot still renders in full
must_not: refuse to render, which withholds the read exactly when the board most needs one
collapse the slice cards into their parent in the displayed counts, which would silently invent a board the forge does not have
propose a split or a merge — this command asks nothing
why_this_fixture_exists: Consolidating is irreversible and belongs to a command that asks first. Refusing is the other tempting answer and is worse. Reporting and rendering anyway is the only outcome that leaves the reader both informed and served.
